page: Microsoft Azure D4ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical AMD EPYC 9V74 cores with multithreading enabled at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 32 MB of L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory and includes a 236 GB local disk, with support for Premium Storage. No GPU resources are included.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is moderate, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores falling in the middle 50%. Memory read bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, registering in the bottom 25% for both small cached and large uncached read operations, though memory write bandwidth and PassMark memory scores remain average. Cryptographic and integer operations perform adequately, as evidenced by average scores in PassMark CPU encryption and Redis SET operations. Complex multi-threaded tasks, such as Clang software compilation and medium-model LLM prompt processing, show weaker performance, with the latter falling into the bottom 10%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D4ads_v6 offers a balanced resource profile for general-purpose workloads, combining dedicated AMD EPYC compute with local storage. The inclusion of a 236 GB local disk reduces the need for external storage attachments for temporary data. This configuration is appropriate for workloads such as static web serving, text processing, and lightweight database operations. However, it is less effective for memory-bandwidth-intensive applications, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference due to the identified memory read bottlenecks and lower multi-threaded scaling.
